A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RIDER/E-RIDER work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original AIHWKit simulations of SP calibration, pulse costs, MNIST and CIFAR-100 training, and chopping sensitivity.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulations and adds ImageNet-1K fine-tuning results and moving-average/residual-parameter sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithms 2–3 retain the same residual-gradient evaluation, moving-average SP tracking, chopping, and periodic synchronization. The expanded device descriptions and additional model evaluation do not change the proposed training procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix F.5 adds reduced-scale ImageNet-1K classification fine-tuning to the retained MNIST and CIFAR-100 coverage. This substantially extends evaluation to a larger, 1,000-class image-recognition setting.

E2.justification: The existing TT-v2 and AGAD comparisons are retained, and AGAD is reused for ImageNet. Appendix F.5 additionally provides pretrained-digital and direct-analog-deployment reference baselines, reporting 70.18% and 63.17% accuracy before analog fine-tuning.

E3.justification: The new ImageNet experiment introduces class-balanced sampling of 200 training images per class, evaluation on all 50,000 validation images, and pretrained VGG-11-BN with only its final two fully connected layers converted to analog using ReRamArrayOMPresetDevice. These are substantial additional evaluation settings; the original MNIST/CIFAR protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F.6 adds focused sensitivity sweeps for moving-average stepsize eta and residual scaling gamma in Tables 9–10, testing tracking responsiveness and residual stability. The existing chopping-probability analysis is retained and relocated, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report three repetitions with sample means and standard deviations for Tables 1–2. v2 adds no repeat-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information; its new Tables 8–10 contain point estimates without additional uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 8 supplies ImageNet comparison results: at reference mean/std 0.05/0.05, E-RIDER achieves 66.41% versus AGAD's 63.82%. Tables 9–10 add sensitivity results, including final accuracy falling from 89.09% at gamma=0.4 to 11.35% at gamma=0.5. These are newly reported results; the original Tables 1–2 are numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem C.4 changes its condition from μ_q < 1/(3 μ_q Δw_min) to μ_q < 1/(3 Δw_min), removing an extra μ_q factor. The main convergence results and accompanying proofs otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about ZS pulse complexity, simultaneous SP tracking and training, RIDER convergence, and E-RIDER efficiency. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining the core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains physical sources of update asymmetry and the device behavior excluded by the response-function assumptions. Appendix F.6 adds parameter-specific applicability guidance, particularly failure at gamma≥0.5, while F.5 interprets the new results as evidence of scaling beyond MNIST/CIFAR.

D1.justification: New Appendix F.1 and Table 3 disclose device presets, numerical variation parameters, and explicit cycle-to-cycle noise modeling. F.5 specifies the ImageNet subset and analog-layer dimensions. The abstract adds a promised code-release location, without establishing that code is available. Existing hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds dataset and architecture citations for ImageNet, VGG, ResNet, CIFAR, and MNIST/LeNet. Its substantive positioning relative to AGAD, residual learning, and zero-shifting remains unchanged; the additional Gong bibliography entry represents the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: v2 expands selected introductory explanations, adds a device-model paragraph, and reorganizes Appendix F around device details, retained settings, ImageNet evaluation, and sensitivity studies. Most existing prose and the overall argument structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds device Table 3 and experimental Tables 8–10. Figure 5 is redrawn and moved from the appendix into the main experiments section. Existing tables are renumbered or repositioned, with otherwise limited changes to the established visual format.

improvement.justification: The ImageNet comparison broadens empirical support, the eta/gamma sweeps reveal useful stability limits, and the device disclosures improve reproducibility. These are concrete gains over v1. Their significance is bounded by the reduced-scale, partially analog ImageNet setup and missing uncertainty and training details for the new experiments; the central algorithms and original results are unchanged.
